key_insight: The paper builds a benchmark framework that maps realistic nuclear many-body Hamiltonians to qubits and compares quantum eigenvalue algorithms on consistent nuclear test problems.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical way to estimate T-gate costs and scalability for Quantum Phase Estimation, Quantum Krylov, and Observable Dynamic Mode Decomposition on nuclear simulation workloads.
method: Map chiral EFT nuclear interactions from second quantization to qubit Hamiltonians.
Construct benchmark instances for no-core and valence-space models with NN and selected 3N interactions.
Estimate resources using Trotterization, Qubitization, and Quantum Singular Value Transformation primitives.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports resource estimates and scaling comparisons across algorithms, system sizes, and model-space choices, focusing on T-gate counts.
watch_item: Results depend on modeling choices such as the Hamiltonian truncation, selected three-body terms, and the specific resource-estimation primitives used.
paper_title: Nuclear Many-Body Systems as Benchmarks for Quantum Computing
